headword: ブラック{企業|きぎょう}
gloss: exploitative company; sweatshop company; abusive employer

definitions.gloss: exploitative company; sweatshop company; abusive employer
definitions.explanation: A company notorious for overworking employees, paying inadequate wages (especially for overtime), engaging in harassment, or otherwise mistreating its workers. A widely used social term in contemporary Japan.

examples.japanese: ブラック{企業|きぎょう}に{勤|つと}めている。
examples.english: I work for an exploitative company.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}はブラック{企業|きぎょう}を{辞|や}めてフリーランスになった。
examples.english: He quit an exploitative company and became a freelancer.

examples.japanese: {長時間|ちょうじかん}{労働|ろうどう}と{残業代|ざんぎょうだい}{未払|みばら}いはブラック{企業|きぎょう}の{典型|てんけい}だ。
examples.english: Long working hours and unpaid overtime are typical of exploitative companies.

examples.japanese: {就職活動|しゅうしょくかつどう}ではブラック{企業|きぎょう}を{避|さ}けるために{口|くち}コミを{調|しら}べた。
examples.english: During my job hunt, I researched online reviews to avoid exploitative companies.

notes:
A widely used contemporary term composed of the English loanword ブラック (black, used here metaphorically as "shady" or "bad") + {企業|きぎょう} (company, enterprise). Coined in the 2000s, it became common in the 2010s alongside growing awareness of labor abuses, overwork, and death-by-overwork ({過労死|かろうし}).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ブラック{企業|きぎょう}に{勤|つと}める: to work at an exploitative company
- ブラック{企業|きぎょう}を{辞|や}める: to quit an exploitative company
- ブラック{企業|きぎょう}{大賞|たいしょう}: "Black Company Grand Prize" (an annual naming-and-shaming award)
- ブラック{企業|きぎょう}の{特徴|とくちょう}: characteristics of a black company

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ホワイト{企業|きぎょう}: white company — the opposite; a company with good working conditions
- ブラックバイト: part-time job with exploitative conditions (especially targeting students)
- {過労死|かろうし}: death from overwork — the extreme consequence associated with such companies

TYPICAL SIGNS:
Commonly cited signs of a ブラック{企業|きぎょう} include unpaid overtime (サービス{残業|ざんぎょう}), very high employee turnover, power harassment, and impossible quotas. The term carries strong negative connotations and is used both in casual complaints and in serious journalism.
